exercise.name: Behind-the-Head Skull Crusher
library_steps: Lie on a flat bench holding a bar or EZ bar above your chest.
Let your upper arms tilt back and lower the bar behind your head.
Straighten your arms to bring the bar back over your chest.
exercise.one_line_summary: Flat bench, head at the bench end, straight bar held palms toward the feet about shoulder width (~40 cm); start arms straight and vertical over the chest; the upper arms tilt back ~45 deg (to 135 deg from the torso) while the elbows bend to ~110 deg, so the bar ends ~5-15 cm past the top of the head at about bench height. Triceps (long head stretched) does the work.

setup.target: Flat, 0 deg; head at the end of the bench so the bar can pass behind it.
setup.tolerance: crown within 0-5 cm of the bench end
setup.why: Library: flat bench. StrengthLog: head near the edge. Outlift lowers the bar to the bench behind the head.

setup.target: Head, upper back and hips on the pad, feet flat.
Palms toward the feet (pronated), thumbs wrapped, wrists straight; hands ~40 cm apart (about shoulder width).
setup.why: StrengthLog: shoulder-width grip; ACE: elbows shoulder-width, neutral wrists.

setup.target: Arms straight and vertical, bar over the chest (nipple line).
setup.tolerance: bar within 5 cm of the nipple line
setup.why: Library step 1 and step 3; Outlift starts each rep over the chest.

movement.measure: upper arm from the torso side line (tilts back, unlike a normal skull crusher)
movement.end: 135 deg (upper arm ~45 deg back past vertical, elbows pointing up and over the face)
movement.tolerance: end 120-150; never flat beside the head (that is a pullover)

movement.measure: 0 = out to the side, +90 = straight up from the chest
movement.end: 88 deg (elbows stay shoulder width, no flare)
~5-15 cm past the crown, at about bench-top height, clear of head and bench
movement.tolerance: clear of head and bench > 0.02 m

movement.start: flat on the pad, wrists straight
movement.tolerance: no rib flare or back arch; wrist bend under 10 deg

muscles.anatomy: Triceps brachii, caput longum, laterale, mediale
muscles.emg: Lying barbell extension 62 % of the triangle push-up (long head 70 %) (S1). Overhead-arm training grew the long head +28.5 % vs +19.6 % neutral (S2). Lowering behind the head raises the arm relative to the torso and stretches the long head (S3, S4).
muscles.role: Straightens the elbow; the arm tilt only adds stretch.

muscles.muscle: Lats / teres major (control the tilted-back arm)
muscles.role: Pull the upper arm back to vertical; too much of this turns it into a pullover (S4).

muscles.muscle: Front delt / chest holding the arm

muscles.role: Grip only; library does not list forearms.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms drop flat beside the head with little elbow bend.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Outlift: too much shoulder movement turns it into a pullover; the triceps stop doing the work.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows wider than the hands at the bottom.
mistakes.why_it_matters: StrengthLog: keep the distance between the elbows constant.

sources.citation: Boehler B, Porcari JP, Kline D, Hendrix CR, Foster C, Anders M. 2011. ACE-sponsored research: best triceps exercises. ACE Certified News, Aug 2011.
sources.what_it_gave: Lying barbell triceps extension 62 % of triangle push-up (long head 70 %).

sources.citation: Maeo S, Wu Y, Huang M, et al. 2023. Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position. Eur J Sport Sci 23(7):1240-1250.
sources.what_it_gave: Overhead arm: long head 1.5x the growth of the neutral arm.

sources.citation: StrengthLog. How to do barbell lying triceps extension.
sources.what_it_gave: Head near the bench edge, shoulder-width grip, bar lowered behind the head (not to the forehead), arms rise relative to the torso to stretch the long head, keep elbow distance constant.

sources.citation: Duquette S, Walker-Ng M. 2024. How to do skull crushers. Outlift.
sources.what_it_gave: Start over the chest, angle the arms backwards, lower to the bench behind the head; elbows moving back adds triceps stretch; too much shoulder movement becomes a pullover.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Exercise Library: Lying Barbell Triceps Extensions.
sources.what_it_gave: Pronated closed grip, elbows shoulder-width, neutral wrists, feet flat; bar may go slightly behind the head.

clip_check.check: Start: arms straight and vertical, bar over the chest
End: upper arms tilted back, elbows bent
End bar 5-15 cm past the crown, not inside head or bench
Hands 30-50 cm apart, palms toward the feet, on the bar
Back on pad, feet on floor, head at the bench end
Triceps strongest red in both pictures
